svg.text: A4 landscape, 1:1 net for one-piece tuck box, 0.3 mm cardstock.
Print at 100% / "Actual size". Do not use "fit to page".
Printed side = inside. Solid = cut, dashed = valley fold, grey = board outline.
1. Print A4 landscape at 100% / "Actual size". Never "fit to page".
2. Check the 100 mm bar. The printed side becomes the inside.
3. Score every dashed line. Cut the solid lines and the openings.
4. Fold the four walls up. Fold the LIP down inside the FRONT wall.
5. Glue the four G tabs to the inside of the FRONT and BACK walls.
6. Drop the board in: J1/J3 at BACK, J2 at FRONT, SW1/SW2 at LEFT.
7. Close the lid, then push the 14 x 6.8 mm TUCK tongue through the
12 x 1.0 mm slit. The LIP behind it catches and holds the tongue.
8. Open by lifting the lid's front edge; the tongue slides back out.
OPENINGS (board mm, x from the left, y from the top)
clearance 0.5 on all four sides (0.3 mm cardstock)
tuck tongue 14.0 wide x 6.8 deep, 2.0 radius tip
tuck slit 12.0 x 1.0, 3.5 below the front rim
inner lip 15.0 x 7.4, behind the slit
The USB-A opening is 7.0 mm tall: a right-angle A shell sits high
on a 1.6 mm board. If yours is taller, trim the 0.8 mm strip above
the opening. The LED and reset holes go through the lid.
If this bar is not 100 mm, the printer scaled the page.
Generated by hardware/rp2040_frisk/scripts/gen_paper_case.py from design.yaml. Board 62.0 x 35.0 mm.
